bihar_raw_news.title: Patna's Gandhi Maidan to host Dussehra with 90-foot Ravana effigy, eco-friendly fireworks
bihar_raw_news.content: Patna's Gandhi Maidan to host Dussehra with 90-foot Ravana effigy, eco-friendly fireworks ANI 18 Oct 2026, 19:37 GMT+10 Patna (Bihar) [India], October 18 (ANI): Patna's Gandhi Maidan is set to host the Dussehra celebration, with a 90-foot effigy of Ravana, an 80-foot effigy of Kumbhakarna and an 85-foot effigy of Meghnad, along with eco-friendly fireworks and elaborate security arrangements. The Ravan Dahan programme, organised by the Patna Dussehra Trust Committee, has been held at Gandhi Maidan for several years. This year, the height of Ravana's effigy has been increased by 10 feet from last year's 80 feet. Speaking about the preparations, Patna Dussehra Trust Committee Chairman Kamal Nopani said that the effigies have been made taller this year and special arrangements have been put in place to minimise pollution and ensure the convenience of visitors. 'This year, the effigies stand at 90 feet for Ravana, 85 feet for Meghnad, and 80 feet for Kumbhakarna. We have been increasing the height by 5 feet each year, and this time, we have added 10 feet. Previously, the Ravana effigy was 80 feet tall; now, it has reached 90 feet. We have also arranged for eco-friendly fireworks to minimise pollution. A separate seating area has been provided for women, and the 'Lanka' structure has been built as a double-story construction this year... We have received confirmation that several dignitaries will attend, including the Governor of Bihar, the Governor of Nagaland, the Chief Minister, the Deputy Chief Minister, as well as various Members of Parliament and other ministers,' Nopani said. This year, 35 Ramlila teams from Delhi have arrived in Patna, adding to the attractions of the celebrations. The event has also been witnessing a considerable gathering of people. A grand procession will also be taken out from Nagababa Thakurbari and will reach Gandhi Maidan in the evening. Considering the large number of devotees and visitors expected to attend the event, the Patna district administration, police and the Dussehra Trust Committee have made extensive security arrangements. Police personnel and magistrates will be deployed at all 14 gates of Gandhi Maidan. CCTV cameras installed at the gates will also be used to monitor the crowd and maintain security. The dignitaries expected to attend the programme include Bihar Governor Syed Ata Hasnain, Nagaland Governor Nand Kishore Yadav, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Choudhary, along with MPs and ministers. The annual Ravan Dahan ceremony is among the major attractions of Patna's Dussehra celebrations, drawing large crowds to Gandhi Maidan. bihar_raw_news.title: NHAI Allocates ₹50 Crore For Wildlife Conservation Along Varanasi-Kolkata Expressway
bihar_raw_news.content: Home / India / Trending / NHAI Allocates ₹50 Crore For Wildlife Conservation Along Varanasi-Kolkata Expressway NHAI has rolled out a wildlife conservation and environmental protection plan along the Varanasi-Ranchi-Kolkata Expressway in Bihar. by Tanvi Shrivastava Updated: October 18, 2026 12:04 PM Share Cover Image Courtesy: Wikimedia Commons The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has allocated around ₹50 crore to Bihar’s Environment, Forest and Climate Change Department to implement an environmental conservation and wildlife mitigation plan along the Varanasi-Ranchi-Kolkata Expressway. The plan aims to protect wildlife habitats, conserve endangered species and improve road safety while supporting connectivity to key religious and tourist destinations, including Bodh Gaya in Gaya district and the Sun Temple at Deo in neighbouring Aurangabad district. Scroll down to know more. NHAI Provides 50 Crore For Wildlife Range Along Varanasi-Kolkata Expressway According to Times of India, the plan covers wildlife habitat improvement, the conservation of selected Schedule I species, soil and water conservation, forest fire management, and monitoring and evaluation. The initiative also includes planting around 45,000 saplings along the expressway corridor. NHAI’s regional office in Patna organised a media tour on Friday to showcase the project’s progress, engineering features and regional significance. Project director Devendra Kumar Bansal told the portal that the 33-km Package VII, being constructed in Bihar’s Gaya district at a cost of ₹1,248 crore, has achieved around 36% physical progress. The stretch runs from Anarban Saleya village to Sangrampur, covering the section between kilometre 151 and kilometre 184. The package is being developed under the Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM). The wildlife conservation plan has been prepared in coordination with the state forest department and the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI). The package includes two elephant underpasses and two animal overpasses to allow wildlife to cross the expressway safely. These structures, along with other mitigation measures, are designed to reduce disruptions to animal movement and improve road safety. Also Read: Video: Mysore Palace Sees Tourist Jam In Long Weekend; Netizens: & Some Still Stuck On Highway& Expressway To Feature Cameras And Trauma Centres To Boost Road Safety The expressway will also feature high-quality cameras installed at one-kilometre intervals to support monitoring and safety. Trauma centres are planned every 30 km to provide timely medical assistance to passengers in case of emergencies. The Varanasi-Ranchi-Kolkata Expressway will begin at Rivasa in Uttar Pradesh’s Varanasi district and pass through Chandauli in Uttar Pradesh before entering Bihar. It will traverse Kaimur, Rohtas, Aurangabad and Gaya districts, followed by several districts in Jharkhand, including Chatra, Hazaribag, Ranchi, Bokaro, Dhanbad and Ramgarh. Also Read: How India Is Using AI To Find Accident-Prone Highway Stretches Before They Turn Deadly The route will then pass through Purulia and Bankura in West Bengal before connecting to Kolkata. Along with improving regional connectivity, the project is intended to provide better access to important religious and tourist destinations while incorporating measures to protect wildlife and the environment. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar education dept to fill 4156 vacant posts on contract - Hindustan Times
bihar_raw_news.content: The state education department has decided to fill as many as 4,156 posts lying vacant in various directorates on a contractual basis, education minister Mithilesh Tiwari said this on Saturday. The move aims to keep administrative and technical work running smoothly until regular recruitments are completed. Bihar education department building (HT Photo) Posts of junior engineers and assistant engineers in the Bihar state educational infrastructure development corporation (BSEIDC), the body responsible for construction, repair and maintenance of school buildings, will also be filled with qualified candidates on contract. Education secretary Rajiv Roushan stressed the urgency of filling these engineering vacancies so that infrastructure work does not stall. A senior officer said that recruitments will be made on class four and class three grades, who include sweepers, cleaners, drivers, lower division clerks and engineers. Tiwari made it clear that the department would rely on contractual appointments in the directorates for the time being. “We will manage with contractual staff until regular appointments are made. The department will assess the final number of vacancies and send requisitions to the concerned recruitment agencies in due course,” he said. Officials indicated the 4,156 vacancies are spread across different levels and directorates under the education department. Read More On the academic side, Tiwari directed officials to ensure textbooks reach every school before the new session begins. “Books must be made available to all children before 1 April so that studies can start without any hitch,” he said. He also instructed that adequate subject-wise teachers be posted in all higher secondary schools so that students do not miss out on any subject. The department has also decided to send a requisition to the Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) to fill up 76 vacant posts of agriculture teachers. The officials have been told to expedite clearance of the pending cases related to retirement, pension, arrears and leave within the stipulated time frame and complete the tendering processes in time so that related works finish before 31 March. In another important move, the minister said, the department would transfer grants for unaided teachers for the first time directly into their bank accounts through direct benefit transfer (DBT), instead of routing the money through school management committees. At a departmental meeting on Friday, the officials also discussed proposed rules and amendments concerning the appointment of secondary school headmasters, municipal teachers, the education clerical cadre and the Sanskrit Education Board. Tiwari told officers to complete all departmental schemes and work within the fixed deadlines so that academic arrangements in schools improve and service-related issues of teachers and staff are resolved promptly. The BPSC has already launched the process to appoint over 33,000 teachers of various classes, for which aspirants have started filling up the forms. The teachers recruitment examination (TRE-4) is likely to be held in March next year. The meeting was attended by education secretary Rajiv Roushan, Bihar School Examination Board (BSEB) chairman Thiyagarajan SM, Bihar education project state project director Navdeep Shukla, Bihar textbook corporation MD Yatendra Kumar

bihar_raw_news.content: NTPC targets 30 GW nuclear capacity by 2047: Water, land, seismic safety and other factors that matter in site selection NTPC plans feasibility studies for nuclear power projects in more Indian states, including Uttar Pradesh. Assessments will consider water supply, land, population, environmental impact, transport, infrastructure, geology, costs, timelines, grid access and electricity demand. Sayak Basu Published 18 Oct 2026, 06:07 PM IST Prefer Livemint on Google AI-generated image. For representational purposes only. AI Quick Read The NTPC is planning to initiate feasibility studies in a number of Indian states for proposed nuclear power projects as part of its drive to expand the generate of enegry from non-fossil-fuel sources to at least 2 GW by 2032, PTI reported citing a senior official. The NTPC, as part of its energy diversification strategy, is targeting to set up 30 GW of nuclear projects in the country to contribute to the government's ambitious 100 GW nuclear capacity target by 2047, as per PTI. A senior official told the news agency that studies in Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Odisha have been carried out, and it will start looking for more locations in other states. Banka in Bihar, Basai in Madhya Pradesh and Nabarangpur in Odisha, the official said, adding, "More states will be explored as the vision is 30 GW nuclear capacity by 2047 . Of course, Uttar Pradesh is on our list along with more states. We will conduct feasibility studies soon." He also revealed that the company's plan is to set up an average project having 1,400 MW with two units of 700 MW each. For a state government, the key question is whether it can offer a technically suitable, environmentally acceptable, and socially feasible site. Here are the key factors the NTPC will examine: 1. Continuous availability of cooling water The ready and uninterrupted supply of water is one of the biggest deciding factors, since conventional nuclear reactors need large, dependable water supplies for cooling as well as heat rejection. Thus, the sites need to be near perennial rivers or reservoirs, or have access to coaster seawater. It should also be ensured that water remains available during droughts and summer months. Competing requirements for drinking water, irrigation, and other industrial needs have to be ascertained. 2. Land availability, population density The NTPC has to look for a sufficiently large, contiguous site with clear ownership and which will also be able to accommodate the plant and its safety-related areas. Adequate land has to be available for reactor units, auxiliary facilities and cooling infrastructure. The population density around the site should be relatively low. The potential project should lead to limited displacement of villages, homes, or agricultural lands. 3. Environmental impact and regulatory clearances The assessment will also consider the possible environmental impact of the project on forests, wildlife habitats, wetlands, groundwater, air and water quality. bihar_raw_news.title: Madhya Pradesh's 1,200 MW Solar-Battery Projects Await Government Nod, Delhi, Haryana ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): Haryana, Delhi and Bihar have agreed to 1,200 MW solar and battery storage projects with Madhya Pradesh. Approval for these projects is pending at the state government level. Once approved and operational, the projects will provide Madhya Pradesh with additional electricity during evening hours, when power demand is at its peak. Sources in the new and renewable energy department said the proposed projects include 500 MW each in partnership with Delhi and Haryana and 200 MW with Bihar. As far as projects with Haryana, Delhi and Bihar are concerned, the generated power will be used by the partner states on a rotational basis. Madhya Pradesh will draw power from October till April, the period during which power demand remains higher. On the other hand, Haryana, Delhi and Bihar would draw power from April till September. Apart from this, Mandsaur's pumped storage project is nearing completion. Its capacity is 1,920 MW. At least 10 more similar projects are in the pipeline in different parts of the state. Projects can be set up in one or two years Additional Chief Secretary for the New and Renewable Energy Department Manu Shrivastava said, We can set up projects within one or two years and supply inexpensive power once the energy department is willing to purchase it. Solar power cheaper than thermal energy The power produced by solar projects is far cheaper than the energy produced by thermal projects. The solar energy rate is Rs 2.15 per unit in comparison to Rs 6 per unit of thermal energy. The installation period for a thermal power plant is at least six years, while solar projects hardly need 12-18 months for their installation. This means that through solar power projects, power generation starts much earlier in comparison to thermal power projects. national_raw_news.title: Truck crash near Sheetla Mata Temple in Gwalior kills 12, injures 39
national_raw_news.content: In Madhya Pradesh, twelve people were killed and 39 others injured after an out-of-control truck crashed into the outer wall of the Sheetla Mata Temple on Chinaur Road in Gwalior last night. The vehicle reportedly broke through police barricades, rolled down a steep slope and ploughed into devotees gathered on the road, crushing several pilgrims before coming to a halt. According to Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Dharmveer Singh Yadav, the accident occurred at around 1.30 AM when a truck loaded with paddy went out of control, hit devotees heading towards the Sheetla Mata Temple and crashed into the temple wall. The impact of the collision also caused the temple wall to collapse, triggering panic at the spot. Police and local residents rushed to the scene, rescued the injured and shifted them to nearby hospitals for treatment. Two police personnel who were on duty at the spot were also injured and are undergoing treatment in the hospital. President Droupadi Murmu and Vice-President CP Radhakrishnan have expressed condolences on the loss of life in a road accident in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh. In a social media post, the President has prayed for the swift recovery of those injured. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also expressed grief at the mishap. Mr Modi has announced an ex-gratia of 2 lakh rupees from the Prime Minister’s National Relief Fund for the next of kin of each of those who lost their lives and fifty thousand rupees for those injured.

national_raw_news.title: Protests over rising living costs, low wages and housing prices sweep Belgium, France, Italy and ...
national_raw_news.content: Hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets across Belgium, France, Italy and Portugal to protest against rising living costs, low wages and the growing difficulty of accessing affordable housing. The demonstrations have put governments across the European Union under pressure. France witnessed widespread unrest, with more than five lakh fifty thousand people participating in demonstrations, according to the Interior Ministry. The protests, which followed weeks of student demonstrations, escalated into clashes, widespread looting and arson as groups of masked protesters targeted shops, historic public buildings and police vehicles. French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said around 1,200 people had been arrested and 150 police officers injured. Dozens of shops were looted in several cities, including Paris, Marseille, Nice, Bordeaux and Toulouse. In Limoges, a fire set by masked protesters largely destroyed the historic town hall. Municipal buildings in Marseille and Lille were vandalised, while a tourist office in Lyon was set ablaze. French President Emmanuel Macron vowed that those responsible would be prosecuted. In Belgium, police used tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters in Brussels and Liège following reports of projectiles being thrown at officers and fires being set. Meanwhile, tens of thousands of people reportedly marched in Portugal’s capital, Lisbon, protesting against rising living costs, low wages and soaring housing prices. Portuguese Parliamentary Affairs Minister Carlos Abreu Amorim said the government would not yield to pressure from street demonstrations, while protesters accused political leaders of being out of touch with their concerns. In Italy, demonstrations in Milan against wars and rising living costs turned violent, with protesters clashing with police, looting shops and setting fire to barricades. Police used tear gas and water cannon to disperse the crowds. According to the LaPresse news agency, at least two police officers were injured and around 50 demonstrators were detained. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni condemned the violence, saying that while demonstrating was a right, setting cities ablaze was unacceptable. Milan Mayor Giuseppe Sala also said that although the protesters’ concerns were understandable, violence against police and damage to public property could not be justified. Clashes were also reported in Bologna, where some demonstrators allegedly threw stones at police.

national_raw_news.title: Asian Para Games 2026 to begin in Japan
national_raw_news.content: The Asian Para Games 2026 will officially open in Aichi-Nagoya in Japan, today, with India aiming to build on its record medal haul at the previous edition. The fifth edition of the continental sporting event will bring together around three thousand athletes from 45 National Paralympic Committees. The Games will continue until 24th of October, with competitions across 18 sports. The opening ceremony today will be held at the Paloma Mizuho Stadium in Nagoya under the theme, “WABI: We Are Beautiful Individuals”. The ceremony is scheduled to begin at 2:30 PM Indian Standard Time. Several competitions, including blind football, para badminton, para table tennis and boccia, are scheduled to begin before the opening ceremony. Para-badminton player Pramod Bhagat and sprinter Simran Sharma will lead the Indian contingent as flag-bearers during the ceremony. Simran has replaced para-table tennis player Bhavina Patel to allow Patel adequate rest ahead of her quarter-final match tomorrow. India has fielded a 281-member contingent, comprising 168 athletes and 113 officials and support staff. The athletes include 112 men and 56 women, who will compete across 11 disciplines. The Indian squad features several prominent para-athletes, including javelin thrower Sumit Antil, para-badminton player Pramod Bhagat, para-shooter Avani Lekhara, para-archer Sheetal Devi, sprinter Simran Sharma and para-table tennis player Bhavina Patel. During the Asian Para Games 2023 at Hangzhou in China, India had secured a record 111 medals, comprising 29 gold, 31 silver and 51 bronze, to finish fifth in the overall standings. The tally surpassed India’s previous record of 72 medals at the 2018 edition in Jakarta. India will now look to build on that historic performance as the country’s para-athletes prepare to compete against the best talent from across Asia.

national_raw_news.title: Kenya’s Charles Matata breaks course record to win men’s elite race at Vedanta Delhi Half Marathon 8 hours ago 150
national_raw_news.content: Kenya’s Charles Matata broke the course record to win the men’s elite race at the Vedanta Delhi Half Marathon today, while Ethiopia’s Wudinesh Alemu claimed the women’s title. Matata clocked 58 minutes, 52 seconds over the 21.097-kilometre course, shaving one second off the previous record set by Ethiopia’s Amedework Walelegn in 2020. Matata set the record to earn an additional 12,000 dollars on top of the 27,000 dollar winner’s prize. Kenya swept the men’s podium, with Samwel Nyamai Mailu finishing second in 59 minutes, 24 seconds and Stanley Waithaka Mburu third in 59 minutes, 33 seconds. Alemu won the women’s race in 1 hour, 6 minutes, 35 seconds. Kenya’s Selah Businei finished second in 1 hour, 7 minutes, 1 second, followed by Cynthia Chelangat Chepkwony in 1 hour, 7 minutes, 32 seconds. In the Indian elite men’s race, Shailesh Kushwaha won in one hour, five minutes and five seconds, ahead of Gaurav Mathur in one hour, five minutes and 11 seconds, and Hemant Kumar in one hour, five minutes and 37 seconds. Ankita Dhyani won the Indian elite women’s title in one hour, 12 minutes and 46 seconds. Soniya finished second in one hour, 14 minutes and 56 seconds, while Bhagirathi was third in one hour, 15 minutes and 51 seconds. Union Minister Kiren Rijiju, Chief of Defence Staff Gen. N.S. Raja Subramani and World Athletics Vice President Adille Sumariwalla attended the event. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta flagged off the Great Delhi Run.
